text:
mira (AE): Heads-up — MeridianBank asked for a quick POC to swap from CompetitorY to Redwood. They currently rely on a server-side session model + per-session system directives. Goal: live demo next Wed, POC by EOW. Main asks: preserve session sticky behavior, minimal client changes, parity on reranker outputs, and enterprise security paperwork. Any immediate blockers?
owen - solutions: Do we have an off-the-shelf compatibility shim for CompetitorY semantics or is this a custom proxy for each customer?
harper (SE): We don’t have a turnkey productized shim. We can build a tiny compatibility proxy that maps CompetitorY session semantics -> Redwood conversation API. CompetitorY flow looks like:
```
POST /session/create
{ "sid": "mb-abc", "system_prompt": "You are an assistant for banking workflows" }
POST /session/message
{ "sid": "mb-abc", "turn": { "role": "user", "text": "Balance for account 123" } }
GET /session/state?sid=mb-abc
```
jordan (sales-eng): MeridianBank uses reranking where they call generate -> collect N candidates -> rerank with an internal model per session. They need deterministic continuation across model variants. Can we expose the same prompt history ordering and deterministic seeds?
harper (SE): Determinism: pin model_revision for POC. Redwood runtime supports deterministic sampling when using top_k/top_p with a fixed seed for inference. We should surface a compatibility flag in the proxy: `X-compat-seed` and set sampler params. Also ensure the history ordering matches (we'll mirror CompetitorY's canonical ordering: system, assistant, user).
security-eng: On the security side: MeridianBank needs KMS-backed key custody (customer-managed), signed DPA, SOC2 Type II, and an answer on whether session metadata is logged. Short answers: yes to KMS (Private or Dedicated), we can provide DPA + SOC2 under NDA, and by default session metadata appears in audit logs but can be redacted for Private deployments. We'll need the customer's security questionnaire filled to map gaps.
mira (AE): They specifically asked whether we can avoid touching the session store — i.e., let them keep session state in their network and pass a token. Is that doable with Redwood hosted?
harper (SE): For hosted: we are stateless and require the conversation state to be passed or reconstructed client-side. Options: 1) Proxy approach where their session token maps to a conversation_id stored in our shim (no client change). 2) Recommend Private deployment so their session store remains on-prem and we call the model locally. For POC, proxy is fastest.
owen - solutions: For the proxy we should support header compatibility: CompetitorY sets `X-Session-Id`, `X-User-Context`, and returns `X-Remaining-Calls`. Redwood uses `X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining`. We'll translate headers to avoid client changes. Note: do not expose internal TTLs or internal metric names.
infra-oncall: Rate-limit behavior: CompetitorY enforces per-session QPS caps; Redwood enforces per-key and per-route quotas. The proxy can track per-session QPS and enforce the same windows in front of Redwood. We'll need to account for burst tokens on Dedicated.
jordan (sales-eng): Pricing question: MeridianBank currently bills per-conversation-turn. They want to know how predictable costs compare with Redwood token billing and Dedicated reserved capacity.
owen - solutions: High-level: per-turn maps to tokens * avg_token_per_turn. For their numbers (est. 200k turns/month, avg 180 tokens/turn), that's ~36M tokens. Hosted per-token billing will be linear; Dedicated can be structured as committed throughput + lower unit price and predictable monthly commitment. I'll prep a short cost comparison by Tue.
mira (AE): Legal also asked about KMS key handling details and the DPA turnaround. What's typical?
security-eng: We provide KMS integration docs and network diagrams. For customer-managed KMS: we support cloud KMS (AWS, GCP) key wraps and HSM via Private. DPA and standard contract redlines are typically 2-3 weeks depending on countersign. We'll flag legal to expect initial docs in 48h after NDA.
harper (SE): POC acceptance criteria suggestion from MeridianBank: 1) no client-side code changes (proxy only), 2) reranker parity within 3% ranking deviation across 10 canonical queries, 3) latency within 20% of current CompetitorY p95. We can run an automated parity harness — propose: 10 canonical prompts, 5 paraphrases each, compute embedding cosine and rank correlation (Spearman rho).
devops-bot: NOTE: create ephemeral workspace `meridian-poc-2026` and grant harper, owen, mira access.
infra-oncall: Also: we should capture KV cache behavior. CompetitorY uses a per-session prefix cache that speeds up subsequent token generation. Redwood's runtime supports prefix caching; for parity enable prefix_cache and pin model_revision. We'll log KV cache hits for the eval run.
jordan (sales-eng): Action items: @harper run parity harness and report similarity metrics by Tue EOD; @owen deliver cost comparison and Dedicated proposal by Tue; @security-eng send questionnaire link + initial KMS doc; @mira schedule demo Wed 2pm ET.
owen - solutions: I'll also scaffold a tiny Node proxy example that shows header mapping, session->conversation mapping, and compatibility headers. Will push to `git.redwood/meridian-poc-proxy` and post link here.
mira (AE): If parity passes, propose a short pilot on Dedicated for 30 days. Will capture SOW needs. Thanks team — will update thread with links and questionnaire responses. :white_check_mark:
